title: Lobbyist registry by-law and Q3 financial update
subtitle: Committee also heard about water and wastewater surpluses, capital spending progress, and accessible taxi and MobilityPLUS vehicle needs.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council approve a by-law and code of conduct for a Regional lobbyist registry {{vote:m2}}. The registry would make public who lobbies Regional councillors and staff, and on what. Staff said it is meant to improve transparency and not to limit residents' access to councillors. A public information campaign begins in December, the registry launches in January, and penalties apply after a six-month grace period.

The committee also recommended that Council receive the Q3 2024 plan and financial update and amend the 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2035 Capital Forecast {{vote:m3}}. Staff reported projected surpluses in both water and wastewater user rates, and said the 2024 capital program is progressing, with about 74% of the budget expected to be spent by year-end.
Because these are committee recommendations, they go to Council for a final decision. The committee's next meeting is December 3, 2024.

decisions.item: Lobbyist registry by-law and code of conduct
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the by-law and code of conduct for the Region's lobbyist registry, as set out in report PDL-CAS-24-006.
The committee recommended that Council receive the third quarter update on the Annual Business Plan and Growing with Care strategic plan progress.
The committee recommended amending the 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2035 Capital Forecast as set out in Appendix D of the report.

debate: One councillor supported a lobbyist registry in principle but questioned whether 2025 was the right year, and asked about the tax impact. Staff said the software, a full-time policy advisor and the registrar were already approved in the 2024 budget.

Another councillor asked how much the registry would cost and how many lobbyists might register. Staff said ongoing cost is mainly the existing staff position, and that no number of registrants can be estimated before the registry opens.

Councillors asked who is responsible if someone lobbies without registering. Staff said responsibility rests with the lobbyist, not councillors or staff, and that the penalties are non-monetary and begin after a six-month grace period.

The mover of the registry motion called it best practice as the region grows, and said some developers had seemed guarded about lobbying registries. Staff clarified the Region would not fund area municipalities' registries but could offer advice. The area municipalities have chosen to delay adopting their own registries for now.

A councillor welcomed growth in accessible taxis but said some recently funded vehicles cannot carry larger mobility devices, and that more money may be needed in the 2025 budget. Staff said they are seeing the same trend in taxis and MobilityPLUS vehicles, such as turning radius issues, and are committed to addressing it.
